newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: HERMIS BANK SAYS SIAULIU HAS GOOD PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: HERMIS BANK SAYS SIAULIU HAS GOOD PROSPECTS.

text.p: Lithuania's Hermis Bank said on Wednesday that its planned acquisition of a majority stake in Siauliu Bank would give it access to a potentially lucrative regional market.

Hermis confirmed on Wednesday that it was seeking to buy 51 percent of Siauliu Bank's shares and that the central bank would consider its application on Thursday. Hermis already has a small stake in Siauliu Bank.
"We are attracted by the fact that Siauliu Bank is a small regional bank which is both stable and profitable," Vytautas Jurna, Hermis Bank's deputy chairman, told Reuters.
Siauliu Bank's net profit in 1996 was 3.9 million litas after posting a loss of 2.9 million litas the previous year.
Jurna said that Hermis Bank also saw the acquisition as a way to get a foothold in Siauliai, which is the site of a planned free economic zone.
"The economy zone will be a business centre and banking services will be required," he said.
He added that Hermis Bank was still mulling the idea of participating in the privatisation the state-run State Commercial Bank.
Analysts and senior central bank officials have predicted that Lithuania's banking sector would witness several mergers and acquisitions this year.
Hermis Bank is Lithuania's second largest private bank and its net profit last year soared to over 27 million litas after it posted a loss of over nine million litas the previous year.
Siauliu Bank is one of the smallest commercial banks operating in the country and is the only regional bank to have emerged from the rubble of last year's banking crisis.
